picked.t: Chinese chocolate persimmon hits record low prices in Vietnam
picked.body: Vendors in HCMC and Hanoi are selling the fruit at up to VND60,000 depending on quality, but at most places it costs around VND30,000, making it 10% lower than other persimmon varieties in Vietnam, including the Da Lat one. The Fuji variety, which originated in Japan but is grown in the Central Highlands, costs three times that price. Chocolate persimmon also originated in Japan but is now grown in several countries including South Korea, China, and Vietnam. The Chinese chocolate variety gets its name from the brown patches or speckles resembling chocolate on the flesh, which become more pronounced as the fruit ripens. It can be eaten even when still firm, has crisp and sweet flesh and no astringency. Some fruits from Shanxi, China, measure 6.5–7.5 centimeters across, have no seeds, and are considered a seasonal specialty. Hoa, a fruit seller in HCMC, said Chinese chocolate persimmons are among her bestsellers because of their unusual appearance, sweetness, and crunch. "I sell two to three boxes a day of 10 kilograms each." In Hanoi, Thanh, a wholesale fruit supplier, said limited supply had kept prices high in previous years. More fruit has arrived this year, driving prices down sharply. In the growing region of Shanxi, wholesale prices for large orders are CNY0.8–1.2 per "jin," a Chinese unit equal to half a kilogram. That works to VND6,000–9,300 per kilogram. Retail prices on Chinese e-commerce platforms are also relatively low. On JD.com, a 1.5-kilogram box of crisp Shanxi chocolate persimmons is advertised at a promotional price of CNY14.9, or about VND38,500 per kilogram. Importers said chocolate persimmon is mainly distributed directly to stores and vendors at traditional markets rather than through wholesale markets. Customs Department data shows Vietnam imported nearly $900 million worth of fruits and vegetables from China in the first eight months of the year, up 51% from the same period last year. Grapes, apples, pears, and persimmons were among the biggest fruit imports.

Terumo Vietnam, VNHA partner on cardiovascular training
picked.body: The partnership will cover medical education, scientific exchange and training in coronary intervention, vascular closure, complex percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) and complication management. It will also include extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO), critical care, and training for catheterization laboratory nurses and other healthcare professionals. Terumo Vietnam will support scientific and educational activities organized by VNHA, providing opportunities for healthcare professionals to update their clinical knowledge, gain practical experience and exchange expertise. Yasuhiro Ikoma, Chief Commercial Officer of Terumo Interventional Systems, said continuous education and knowledge exchange are important to improving patient outcomes. "At Terumo, we believe that empowering healthcare professionals through continuous education and knowledge exchange is essential to improving patient outcomes," he said. "Our collaboration with VNHA reflects Terumo's long-term commitment to supporting healthcare professionals, advancing cardiovascular practice, and contributing to better patient care in Vietnam." Professor Pham Manh Hung, president of VNHA, said continued professional development is important as cardiovascular practices evolve. "Continuous professional development is essential to advancing cardiovascular practice and improving patient outcomes. We highly appreciate Terumo's commitment to supporting educational initiatives that expand learning opportunities and strengthen clinical expertise for healthcare professionals across Vietnam," Dr. Hung said. Nguyen Do Bao Chau, General Director of Terumo Vietnam Medical Equipment, said the partnership would focus on practical training to address changing clinical needs. "By working closely with VNHA, we aim to deliver practical educational initiatives that support healthcare professionals in addressing evolving clinical needs and advancing cardiovascular care across the country," she said. Founded in 1992, VNHA is a nonprofit professional organization in cardiovascular medicine, with activities spanning continuing medical education, research, professional development and international cooperation. Tokyo-headquartered Terumo operates in more than 160 countries and regions, providing medical technologies for areas including vascular intervention, cardiovascular surgery, blood transfusion and cell therapy.
